architecture: v2 (an English mutual motor insurer's 2027 rating bands: which three of its eight rating regions go in the top frequency band, by the claim frequency each region's policies show over the 2024 and 2025 accident years once an at-fault claim no longer moves a policy down the no-claims steps, when policyholders on the middle steps today pay small at-fault damage themselves rather than lose steps)
slot_note: re-rooted 2026-10-19 after architecture 1 was spent at stage 4; the slot takes no seed world (DA20 went to task269's third architecture)
niche: a no-claims step scale makes an at-fault claim cost a policyholder future premium that depends on the step they stand on, so drivers on the middle steps pay small damage themselves; the frequency a region will show once the 2027 wording removes that cost is recovered from the claims nobody absorbs and the size distribution of the policyholders for whom a claim already costs nothing
answer: Band C of the 2027 rating basis holds North West, West Midlands and Yorkshire and the Humber; South East is the first region below.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who builds each region's 2024 and 2025 earned vehicle-years and accident claims correctly (the policy system migration and its crosswalk, mid-term moves between regions, the 1 April 2025 region map change, fault settled, split or pending, windscreen, theft and fire claims out, legacy amounts in pence) ranks the regions by their reported claim frequency, or lifts steps 6 to 9 by the Step Protection holders' frequency against other policyholders on those steps, and files band C as South East, West Midlands and Yorkshire and the Humber; only recovering the claims the middle steps kept back, from the claims above the size no policyholder absorbs and the share of claims that large among step 0 and Step Protection policies, puts North West in band C.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each region's claim frequency under a wording where an at-fault claim costs no no-claims steps, the actuary's frequency of accidents above the excess recovered through the bonus-hunger truncation that a step scale imposes on reported claims (claims every policyholder reports, scaled by the ground-up size distribution of those for whom a claim already costs nothing); with another field's nouns there is no step scale making the cost of a claim depend on the claimant's own step, so nothing is absorbed and nothing is recovered.
layer1: the 2025 move from the legacy policy system to the new platform, policies renumbered at their first platform renewal and joined through a crosswalk, claims notified after that renewal registered under the new number
mid-term adjustments that move a car to another postcode district or change its cover, exposure split by days (a district on the legacy system, a full postcode on the platform)
the legacy expiry date the last day on cover against the platform's renewal date, and cancellation dates on each system's own convention
claims with fault settled, split or pending, not-at-fault claims recovered from the other insurer, nil notifications and rejected third-party claims
amounts in pence on the legacy claims system and pounds on the platform
two postcode districts reassigned between rating regions from 1 April 2025
notification times in UTC on the platform against UK dates elsewhere
stakeholder_role: the mutual's pricing actuary, preparing the 2027 rating basis for the pricing committee

spine.entity: one policy year on the legacy system
spine.row_meaning: a private car policy's cover over one policy year: inception and expiry, cancellation, garaging district, step and Step Protection at inception, cover, car, premium
spine.source_dataset: constructed (seeded generator; the mutual, its partner firms and people are fictional)

world.geography: United Kingdom, England and Wales (a fictional mutual motor insurer)

driver: The decisive quantity is how often each group's members will report an event once reporting costs them nothing, when today each member absorbs events smaller than what reporting would cost them and that cost rises and falls with their position on a scale, so the reported count understates most the groups whose members stand where reporting costs most; counting only the events too large for anyone to absorb, scaled by how common events that large are among members for whom reporting already costs nothing, recovers it, while a group that buys out the cost is self-selected and gives the size of events, not their rate.
driver_concrete: Each region's claims per 100 vehicle-years under the 2027 protected wording, recovered step by step from the at-fault claims above the size no policyholder absorbs, scaled by the share of claims that large among step-0 policyholders and Step Protection holders, plus the not-at-fault claims everyone already makes; the reported frequency and a lift taken from the Step Protection holders' frequency on steps 6 to 9 leave the middle-step regions understated.
stump: A competent solver ranks the regions by their 2024 and 2025 reported claim frequency (or lifts steps 6 to 9 by the Step Protection holders' frequency) and files band C as South East, West Midlands and Yorkshire and the Humber, South East in place of North West, because North West's policyholders stand mostly on the middle steps with the book's highest premiums, where a claim costs the most premium over the climb back, and pay small at-fault damage themselves, so North West reports the smallest share of its accidents while South East, on the top steps and under Step Protection, reports nearly all of its own.

differentiation.task255: task255 fits a severity tail through a floor recorded on every claim (the member's deductible) and a ceiling (the retention) to set a retention; here the decisive quantity is a frequency, the floor is the policyholder's own unrecorded choice driven by the cost of a claim at their step, and the recovery counts claims above the size nobody absorbs against the size distribution of policyholders for whom claiming costs nothing
differentiation.task267: task267 reweights the verified by a verification probability the referral rule fixed; here nothing is verified and no probability is known: the absorbed claims never reach the record and are recovered through their size
differentiation.task180: task180 recovers small events masked by daytime noise from the quiet hours' record and a magnitude law; here the masking is a choice the policyholder makes against a premium scale, its depth set by the step, and the recovery is nonparametric in size
differentiation.task262: task262 removes transitory variance from a single-year reading; here nothing is noisy, events are missing below a size, and which ones depends on the scale step
differentiation.task270: architecture 1 corrected each component's validity for selection on the appointment composite; here no one is selected on a score: claims are absorbed below a cost that the no-claims scale fixes step by step
differentiation.task192: task192's third architecture corrects an instrument's labels with error rates from a validation batch that covered only the window's opening; here no record is mislabelled: claims below a cost the step scale fixes never reach the record, and they are recovered through claim size from the policyholders for whom a claim costs nothing

lineage.niche: the predictive validity of a civil-service police entry examination's components across the candidate pool, estimated from an academy outcome that exists only for the candidates appointed in rank order of two of the components
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how strongly each of several measures predicts an outcome across a whole pool when the outcome exists only for the members picked from the pool in rank order of a weighted sum of two of the measures; the correlations among those picked understate every measure, and correcting each measure as if it alone had picked them leaves the two that formed the sum understated, so only a correction that models the pick on the sum, with the measures' spread across the whole pool, restores which measures predict best.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each examination component's correlation with the police academy's final average across everyone who sat the 2024 and 2025 examinations, recovered from the appointees' grades by the multivariate correction on the written test, the oral board, the veterans' credit and the physical ability test's points the appointments were made on; the appointees' own correlations and a per-component Case II correction both leave the written test and the oral board looking weaker than they are and keep the work style inventory.
lineage.stump: A competent solver correlates each component with the academy final average among the appointees, or corrects each correlation separately by Case II, and keeps the written test and the work style inventory, because the appointments were made in rank order of the written test and oral board composite, which restricted those two (and the oral board most, beside the written test it was ranked with) far more than the per-component spreads show.
lineage.answer: The 2027 entry examination should keep the written test and the oral board.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-19 at stage 4 (Gate F): both isolated scored readers landed the call, the order and the first component below; reader 1 applied the multivariate correction for selection on the variables the appointments were ranked on (Lawley) from the filed rules and the plan's pool, reader 2 the same correction; reader 1 also landed all five costs (5 of 14 ask figures), reader 2 all 14; the judge DETERMINISTIC, APPROVE. A filed selection rule plus a filed population of appointees and non-appointees hands a strong reader the textbook correction.

notes: Re-rooted 2026-10-19. Prototype in scratch (t270b/proto2.py, tune3.py): with a step scale whose claim cost peaks on the middle steps (a claim moves a policy down three steps), thresholds bounded at 1.3 times the step's cost and lognormal damage above a GBP 250 excess, the analytic search found region sets where the protected-wording top three and the reported top three differ by one region with margins of 7 to 10 per cent and the Step Protection lift lands a third set; the build tunes one at stage 3 and asserts every route.
